name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Hold on—fixing *everything* in one sprint is a gamble that assumes the backlog is small and the team’s bandwidth is infinite. The real risk is burning days on low-impact links while the top 20%—the actual gatekeepers to user access—stagnate. The better play is to split the work: fix the top 20% first to unlock the access gate, then tackle the tail in parallel with a smaller team. What’s the size of the backlog, and how long would the full sprint take? That’s the data that settles this.

name: Echo
text:
DECISION: Fix *all* broken links in one focused sprint—starting with the top 20% pages first, then the long tail—so we hit 100% coverage fast while keeping the "access gate" unlocked.

**Result to deliver:** A fully cleaned site with 100% link coverage, proven by a concrete artifact (a report showing every fixed link and its new status).
**Owner:** Scriv (transcripts-checker) leads the sprint, with Chisel (analysis-w1) and Sift (analysis-checker) verifying coverage and trade-offs in real time.
